description:
crate-jmap-chat-types/src/message.rs:240 declares `DeliveryReceipt` with all four fields as `Option<UTCDate>` / `Option<ReadDisposition>`. The natural zero state — "nothing acknowledged yet" — is all-None.

The diff already shipped exactly this pattern on `ChatStreamDisable` in ephemeral.rs (now `#[derive(... Default ...)]` because all fields are optional), so the precedent is set within the same crate and the same review scope.

Idiomatic Rust: any struct whose every field is `Option<_>` (or `Vec<_>` etc. with a sensible empty default) should derive `Default`. Today, a consumer constructing a fresh `DeliveryReceipt` to start populating must write:

    DeliveryReceipt { delivered_at: None, device_delivered_at: None, read_at: None, read_disposition: None, extra: serde_json::Map::new() }

With `Default` derived:

    DeliveryReceipt::default()

The extras field is `serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>` which is `Default`, so the derive is mechanical. No new dependencies, no API breaking change (Default is purely additive).

Workspace AGENTS.md "Idiomatic Rust → type-design" calls this out: "Missing derives: ... Default on types with a sensible zero." The empty-receipt case is exactly the sensible zero.
title: DeliveryReceipt has four Option fields and no Default derive
